name: P ZERO Race TLR 4S

origin.basis: Italian tire maker; Pirelli says the P ZERO Race range is made at its plant in Italy near its Milan headquarters.

manufacturing.basis: Pirelli: the P ZERO Race range is made in Italy (Bollate factory).

positioning: Year-round tubeless racing tire with the SmartNET Silica compound for wet grip and mileage.
pressure_note: The product page gives no maximum pressure; use the figure printed on the tire.

wet_notes.summary: Pirelli describes SmartNET Silica as its best formulation for wet grip, for year-round racing.

availability.note: Listed in Pirelli's UK catalogue with a dealer finder; no mainland China listing was checked for this line; North American availability not verified in this pass.

caveats: Heavier and slower-rolling than the standard P ZERO Race TLR in the same lab; measured wet grip was similar (76 versus 75 at 28 mm).
Hookless compatibility and maximum pressure are not stated on the product page.

image.shown: P ZERO Race TLR 4S sidewall as pictured in Pirelli's catalogue; one photo covers every width.
image.alt: Close-up of a Pirelli P ZERO Race TLR 4S road tire sidewall

rights.usage_note: The maker's own product photo, shown from the maker's website; no copy is stored or redistributed by this project, and no license is asserted.

owner_evidence.screening_note: Coded on 2026-11-04 from a fixed source set: the written reviews on the Sigma Sports and bike-components product pages, read in full through each page's own review list (the newest 15 per page when more exist), every reader comment on Bicycle Rolling Resistance's test pages for this tire, and owner comments in coded Xiaohongshu threads. Counted only owners who describe their own riding; star-only ratings, reviews without riding detail, mounting-only impressions and repeats were left out. Comments on one construction's test page count for that construction unless the owner names the other.

reports.summary: A great tire once fitted that holds air extremely well, though very tight to mount.
More confidence on the road after replacing the bike's original tires.
No issues over a few months; grips well and feels fast.
Does not feel slow and feels strong; on the rear the wear indicator is barely visible at 4,600 km, far longer than a Corsa N.EXT TLR lasted.
Truly amazing grip in pouring rain, but noticeably slower than the GP5000 S TR and the standard P ZERO Race TLR; one plugged puncture in about 4,000 km.

checks.note: One of 4 written reviews describes only fitting and width
